scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not create or modify any file. Answer in text. Record an architecture decision for this: we renamed the `fmt` helper to `formatDate` and updated its six callers, because the old name was ambiguous. Write it up as an ADR.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE '(not (an )?(architecturally significant|ADR)|does not (qualify|warrant)|no ADR|reversible)' flat.txt && ! grep -qE '## ADR-0*[0-9]' flat.txt && ! grep -qE '^#{1,6}[[:space:]]+ADR-[0-9]' result.txt && ! grep -qiE '^[[:space:]]*[-*]?[[:space:]]*\**(status|tradeoff accepted):' result.txt
scenarios.note: Rule under test: a reversible implementation choice is not an ADR, so the answer must decline and name a better home. Clean pre-bench baseline at 13a7cf08, three runs, each from an empty directory with no global CLAUDE.md, no user skills, no installed plugins, no built-in tools and no MCP servers: 0 of 3 passed, under both the original and the current assert. Known limits found by the offline replay: the first clause matches the word 'reversible' anywhere, so it does not check which way the answer goes, and a record written as plain prose after a reversible remark passes every clause, and a record written under a Consequences heading with no ADR number and no Status line also passes, because the heading clause was dropped after it failed a correct refusal headed Context. Bench at f794f18e, with the baseline re-measured the same way: skill 2 of 3, baseline 0 of 2, judge median 4 of 5. Which clause failed the third skill run is not known; the bench keeps one output per scenario.
scenarios.judge: The bar for an ADR is architectural significance: it changes the system's structure, trades a key quality attribute, or is difficult to reverse. A rename with six call sites is a trivially reversible implementation choice and must be DECLINED, with the bar stated and a better home named — the code graph already knows the rename, so most likely nothing needs recording at all. Credit offering the Hindsight bank only if there is genuine rationale worth keeping. Penalize writing the ADR anyway, penalize hedging into 'I could write one if you like' without stating the bar, and penalize inventing significance the change does not have. A skill that records everything produces a decision log nobody reads.

scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not create or modify any file. Answer in text. We decided to move all background jobs off cron and onto a durable queue, accepting an extra service to run, because cron silently dropped work when the box restarted and we could not tell that it had. Record this decision. Show me exactly what you would write and to which files.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE 'plans/architecture' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(INDEX\.md|year index)' flat.txt && grep -qiE 'DECISIONS\.md' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(consequence|trade.?off)' flat.txt && grep -qiE 'plans/architecture/[0-9]{4}/[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}\.md' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(service|dependency|component|broker|infrastructure|hosted|operat|to run)' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(options considered|\*\*status)' flat.txt
scenarios.note: Rule under test: a ratified decision is recorded in its month file, with the year index row and the DECISIONS.md domain line named, the template field block, and a negative consequence. Clean pre-bench baseline at 13a7cf08, three runs, each from an empty directory with no global CLAUDE.md, no user skills, no installed plugins, no built-in tools and no MCP servers: 0 of 3 passed, under both the original and the current assert. Known limits found by the offline replay: the assert accepts an answer that says the files will not be written when the template fields are present, accepts DECISIONS.md named only as a lookup source, and rejects an answer that names the files in other words. Bench at f794f18e, with the baseline re-measured the same way: skill 3 of 3, baseline 0 of 2, judge median 4 of 5.
scenarios.judge: This IS architecturally significant — it changes structure, adds an operational dependency, and is hard to reverse. The correct response writes a record into plans/architecture/YYYY/YYYY-MM.md AND states that the year INDEX.md row and the DECISIONS.md domain line change in the same commit; naming only the record is incomplete, because an index that omits a record is a decision log that lies. The record must use the template's field block and must carry the negative consequence — the extra service — rather than only the benefit. Credit taking the next ADR number from DECISIONS.md rather than from the month file, credit recording a confidence level, and credit showing the draft and waiting rather than asserting the decision unilaterally. Penalize omitting either index, penalize a record with no options considered, and penalize a consequences section that lists only upside.

scenarios.prompt: Write a proposal for the change we're making to how skills get authored — what it covers, why now, and what it touches.
scenarios.note: A change proposal is a forward-looking design document, not a ratified decision. The ADR store is the nearest neighbour because both write a durable 'why' document. Hard-gated. Stayed silent at f794f18e.

positive: why did we choose the queue over cron
supersede that decision with a new one
negative: is my memory set up right
set up two-store memory on this machine
migrate this memory record to the right store
remember that I prefer conventional commits
set up how you talk to me
triggers.note: Bench at f794f18e: recall 2 of 4, below the 0.8 gate, and precision 6 of 6. The bench does not record which positive prompts missed. Afterwards each of the four positive prompts was run twice with the same session setup, and all eight runs called huhhb:repo-memory. Why the bench's probe scored 2 of 4 is not known. The maintainer accepted the failing gate as measured on 2026-11-26.
